study_type_evidence.quote: To assess pharmacokinetics, wild type Sprague Dawley rats were injected with a bolus dose of 50 µg tag-free rhMFG-E8
the lyophilized protein was reconstituted with pure water and subjected to PS binding and cell adhesion assays

in_vivo_species.quote: Sprague Dawley rats (275-350 g) were obtained from Charles River Laboratories.
C57BL6 mice were purchased from Jackson Laboratory.

in_vitro_detail: Phosphatidylserine binding and cell adhesion assays for stability over 2 years of storage.

agents.name: tag-free rhMFG-E8 (beta phase, 2-6 h fit)
agents.sequence_source: Not printed in the body; sequence is PEPlife2's (human MFG-E8 precursor).
agents.group_n_quote: The terminal elimination half-life (t1/2) of the tag-free rhMFG-E8 was calculated for each of 4 independent experiments and averaged.
agents.dose_route_quote: wild type Sprague Dawley rats were injected with a bolus dose of 50 µg tag-free rhMFG-E8
agents.pk_quote: Tag-free rhMFG-E8's average α phase (distribution) t1/2 was 11.55 min, and its average β phase (elimination) t1/2 was 1.45 h

concentration_time_figure.caption_quote: Tag-free rhMFG-E8 has suitable pharmacokinetics in healthy animals. Rats were iv injected with tag-free MFG-E8 and blood samples collected at different timepoints.
concentration_time_figure.note: The alpha phase is designated as 0-0.5 h and the beta phase as 2-6 h; a non-compartmental log-linear trapezoidal analysis in PKSolver was run in parallel.

bioanalytical_method: Human MFG-E8 Quantikine ELISA (R&D Systems MFGE80), which does not cross-react with rat MFG-E8; non-compartmental analysis in PKSolver
bioanalytical_quote: The levels of the tag-free rhMFG-E8 from rat blood samples were measured by Human MFG-E8 Quantikine ELISA kit (R&D Systems, Cat: MFGE80). There is no cross-reaction between human and rat MFG-E8 in this kit.
notes: UNITS ERROR IN PEPlife2, now corrected. The body states the distribution half-life is 11.55 MINUTES; PEPlife2 recorded 11.55 with units 'Hours' (ID 4377), a 60-fold overstatement that also made the distribution phase eight times LONGER than the elimination phase it precedes - an impossibility the record's own numbers should have flagged. Corrected to minutes via UNITS_CORRECTIONS in subset_in_vivo_half_life.py, giving 0.1925 h. That record was in any case already excluded from the training set twice over: PEPlife2 leaves its Sequence field empty, and its phase is distribution rather than a concentration-decay terminal value. The two elimination values are NOT independent measurements: 1.45 h is the beta phase fitted over the 2-6 h window and 2.33 h is the SAME data refitted out to 12 h. The paper's own conclusion is hedged accordingly - 'the beta phase t1/2 of the tag-free rhMFG-E8 is calculated as at least 1.45 h'. Treating them as two observations double-counts one experiment and inflates the apparent spread. n is four independent experiments, not four animals.
